study_material.title: Phrasal Verbs - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: A phrasal verb combines a verb with a preposition or adverb to create a meaning you cannot guess from the parts: 'give up' means quit, not donate upward. Placement papers test the most common ones in fill-in-the-blank and substitution formats.
learning_objectives: Recognise phrasal verbs and their idiomatic meanings
Handle multiple meanings of the same phrasal verb
Use separable and inseparable phrasal verbs correctly
Choose the right particle for the intended meaning

concepts.heading: 1. Why They Are Tricky
concepts.body: The meaning is idiomatic: 'look up' can mean improve ('things are looking up') or search ('look up a word'). The same verb changes completely with different particles: run into (meet), run out of (exhaust), run over (hit with a vehicle), run through (rehearse).

concepts.heading: 2. Separable vs Inseparable
concepts.body: Separable phrasal verbs allow the object between the parts: 'turn the light off' or 'turn off the light'. If the object is a pronoun, separation is COMPULSORY: 'turn it off' - never 'turn off it'. Inseparable verbs keep the parts together: 'look after the baby', never 'look the baby after'.

concepts.heading: 3. High-Frequency List (Part 1)
concepts.body: Break down = stop functioning / lose emotional control. Bring up = raise a child or raise a topic. Call off = cancel. Carry out = perform. Come across = find by chance. Cut down on = reduce. Do away with = abolish. Fall back on = rely on as a reserve. Get along with = have a good relationship.

concepts.heading: 4. High-Frequency List (Part 2)
concepts.body: Give in = surrender. Give up = quit. Hold on = wait. Look after = take care of. Look forward to = anticipate happily. Look into = investigate. Put off = postpone. Put up with = tolerate. Run out of = exhaust supply. Take after = resemble a relative. Turn down = reject or reduce volume. Turn up = arrive unexpectedly. Work out = exercise or find a solution.

concepts.heading: 5. Particle Logic
concepts.body: Particles carry loose patterns that aid memory. UP often means completion or increase (finish up, speed up, use up). DOWN suggests reduction (cut down, calm down). OFF suggests separation or cancellation (call off, take off). OUT suggests exhaustion or emergence (run out, find out). ON suggests continuation (carry on, hold on).

formulas: Pronoun objects force separation: 'turn it off'
Look after = care for; Look into = investigate; Look for = search
UP = completion/increase; DOWN = reduction; OFF = cancellation
Put off = postpone; Put up with = tolerate
shortcut_methods: Learn phrasal verbs in sentences, never as isolated pairs
Group them by shared verb (get, take, put) or shared particle (off, up)
Substitute a single-word synonym to test whether an option fits
common_mistakes: Placing a pronoun after the particle ('turn off it')
Confusing look after / look into / look for
Mixing up put off (postpone) with put up with (tolerate)
Guessing the meaning literally from the two words
study_material.summary: Memorise the high-frequency set in context, respect separability rules for pronouns, and use particle patterns as memory aids.
quick_revision_notes: Call off = cancel; Put off = postpone
Take after = resemble; Look after = care for
Run out of = exhaust; Come across = find by chance

solved_examples.question: Choose the meaning of 'give up': 'He decided to give up smoking.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: 'Give up' followed by an activity means to stop doing it permanently.

solved_examples.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: 'The match was ___ due to rain.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: 'Call off' means to cancel - the standard verb for cancelled matches.

solved_examples.question: Choose the meaning of 'take after': 'She takes after her mother.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: 'Take after' means to resemble an older family member in looks or character.

solved_examples.question: Choose the correct sentence.
solved_examples.step_by_step: With separable phrasal verbs, a pronoun object must sit between the verb and the particle.
solved_examples.shortcut: Pronoun always goes in the middle.

solved_examples.question: Choose the correct phrasal verb: 'I cannot ___ his constant complaining any longer.'
solved_examples.step_by_step: 'Put up with' means to tolerate. 'Put off' is postpone, 'put down' is criticise or set down, 'put across' is communicate.
solved_examples.shortcut: Three-word phrasal verbs are inseparable: put up with something.

practice_questions.question: 'Look after' means:
practice_questions.explanation: Look after = care for someone or something.

practice_questions.question: 'Put off' means:
practice_questions.explanation: Put off = delay to a later time.

practice_questions.question: 'Hold on' means:
practice_questions.explanation: Especially on the phone, 'hold on' means wait a moment.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The car ___ on the highway and we had to call a mechanic.'
Fill in the blank: 'The police are ___ the matter thoroughly.'
Fill in the blank: 'We have ___ milk; please buy some.'
practice_questions.explanation: Run out of = exhaust the supply.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The doctor advised him to ___ his sugar intake.'
In 'Things are looking up after a difficult year', 'looking up' means:
practice_questions.explanation: 'Look up' can mean improve when the subject is a situation.

practice_questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The committee decided to ___ the outdated regulation.'
practice_questions.explanation: Do away with = abolish or get rid of.

topic_test.title: Phrasal Verbs - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Substitute a single-word synonym to test each option.

questions.question: 'Give in' means:
questions.explanation: Give in = yield or stop resisting.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'I am ___ meeting you next week.'
questions.explanation: Look forward to = anticipate with pleasure.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'She was ___ by her grandparents in Kerala.'
Fill in the blank: 'The company ___ his proposal without discussion.'
'Carry out' means:
questions.explanation: Carry out an order or experiment = execute it.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He ___ at the party without an invitation.'
Fill in the blank: 'If the plan fails, we can always ___ our savings.'
questions.explanation: Fall back on = rely on as a reserve option.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The two colleagues ___ very well despite their differences.'
questions.explanation: Get along (with) = have a harmonious relationship.

questions.question: In 'It took her months to get over the illness', 'get over' means:
questions.explanation: Get over = recover from illness or a setback.
